status: G4 rest: processed, compressed and reviewed; ships as g4-sheep-grazing, in Chapters VIII and X (the desktop app only)
use: A grazing sheep of the camp's flock, its head down, by the loom in the court beyond the board (Chapters VIII and X), between the standing sheep.

generator.prompt: A sheep of a Roman camp's flock, mid-3rd century AD, grazing: standing with all four legs straight and evenly spaced, its neck lowered and its muzzle down at ground level as if cropping grass, short tail hanging down, symmetrical. A sturdy hornless ewe about 0.75 metres at the shoulder with a thick oatmeal-brown fleece in tight curls, a dark brown face and dark brown lower legs. No collar, no bell, no people. Realistic proportions, anatomically accurate. Single isolated model with complete geometry from every side and a bold, solid, readable silhouette from above. No ground plane, no display plinth, no text or inscriptions, no modern objects, no fantasy elements.

review.scope: Tripo's own render, four views of the final compressed model with a 1.8 m figure for scale (scripts/assets/preview-model.mjs), and the camps in the desktop build at High
review.notes: As asked: an oatmeal-brown fleece, a dark brown face and legs, its muzzle down at the grass. It came facing its +z and was turned a quarter round: 1.14 m long and 0.8 m high. In Chapter VIII's camp it grazes by the loom between the two white sheep, the darker of the three.
